page: OVHcloud c3-32 is a compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with 16 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The virtualization layer is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in single-core processing, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng falls within the average range. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top 25%, although raw memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes register average results. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing benchmarks also demonstrate strong execution speeds, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput remain average.

With its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c3-32 offers a balanced profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, text processing, multi-threaded decompression, and lightweight LLM inference using smaller models. The inclusion of local NVMe storage supports fast read and write operations for local caching and application execution. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation ensures predictable performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core instances.
